Description

Gs-coupled receptors raise cAMP in dorsal horn neurons and release the catalytic subunits of PKA. PKA increases neuronal excitability, in part by inhibiting A-type K+ currents through ERK, and it recruits GluN2B NMDA receptors and GluA1 AMPA receptors to synapses. These changes add to the central sensitisation found in OA pain.

Colour

Each block is coloured by its effect on pain, red where it raises pain and blue where it relieves it, and everything in it takes that colour, GTP and GDP included, as it works for the block's result. Drugs are yellow and classes of molecules white.

This block is red: PKA reduces glycinergic inhibition in the dorsal horn.

Spinal PGE2 removes glycinergic inhibition through EP2 and PKA phosphorylating GlyR α3. In knee OA the spinal cAMP-PKA pathway is also shown in the other direction, in GABAergic neurons carrying analgesia (Yuan 2021): the colour holds for the neuron drawn.
